title: OAuth / SSO / SAML
summary: redirect_uri, state, PKCE, code reuse, token leakage, SAML signatures, and RelayState.

checks.title: redirect_uri exact match
checks.why: The authorization server accepts a prefix, subdomain, or parameter on redirect_uri and delivers the code off-origin.
checks.validate: A code or token lands on an origin you control.

variants.name: Prefix / path suffix
variants.payload:
GET /authorize?client_id=<id>&redirect_uri=https://app.example.com.evil.example/&response_type=code&state=wapt HTTP/1.1
Host: idp.example.com
Connection: close
variants.expect: Must reject. Also try https://app.example.com/callback/../off and https://app.example.com%40evil.example/.

variants.name: Parameter pollution
variants.payload:
GET /authorize?client_id=<id>&redirect_uri=https://app.example.com/cb&redirect_uri=https://evil.example/&response_type=code&state=wapt HTTP/1.1
Host: idp.example.com
Connection: close
variants.expect: Duplicate redirect_uri must not pick the attacker value.

variants.name: Open redirect on the client
variants.payload:
GET /login?next=https://evil.example/ HTTP/1.1
Host: www.example.com
Connection: close
variants.expect: Post-login next= is a second hop. Must not land off-origin after a good redirect_uri.

checks.title: state and nonce binding
checks.why: The callback accepts a missing, reused, or attacker-chosen state, so login CSRF or code injection works.
checks.validate: A callback without the initiating state's value still establishes a session.

variants.name: Drop state
variants.payload:
GET /callback?code=<code>&state= HTTP/1.1
Host: www.example.com
Cookie: session=<pre-login>
variants.expect: Must fail. Also try omitting state entirely.

variants.name: Replay someone else's state
variants.payload: Start login as A, capture state. Complete B's login with A's state (or a random string).
variants.expect: Must fail. nonce on the id_token must match the initiating session too.

checks.title: PKCE on public clients
checks.why: A public / SPA / mobile client can skip PKCE, or the server accepts any verifier.
checks.validate: An authorization code is exchanged without the matching code_verifier.

variants.name: Omit PKCE on authorize
variants.payload:
GET /authorize?client_id=<spa-id>&redirect_uri=https://app.example.com/cb&response_type=code&state=wapt HTTP/1.1
Host: idp.example.com
Connection: close
variants.expect: A public client must be rejected without code_challenge=S256.

variants.name: Wrong verifier
variants.payload:
POST /token HTTP/1.1
Host: idp.example.com
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

grant_type=authorization_code&code=<code>&redirect_uri=https://app.example.com/cb&client_id=<spa-id>&code_verifier=wrong
variants.expect: Must fail. A success means PKCE is not enforced.

checks.title: Authorization code reuse
checks.why: The same code is exchanged twice, or the code leaks into Referer / logs via a query redirect.
checks.validate: A second exchange issues tokens, or the code is visible on a third-party request.

variants.name: Replay the code
variants.payload: Exchange the code once, then replay the same /token POST.
variants.expect: Second use must fail and should revoke the first grant.

variants.name: Code in Referer
variants.payload: Land on the redirect_uri that still has ?code= in the query, then load a third-party script/image.
variants.expect: The code must not appear in Referer. Prefer a form_post response mode or an immediate 302 that strips it.

checks.title: Tokens out of the URL
checks.why: implicit / hybrid fragments, access_token in a query, or tokens in logs.
checks.validate: A token is observable in a URL, Referer, or a client log you are allowed to read.

variants.name: Reject implicit
variants.payload:
GET /authorize?client_id=<id>&redirect_uri=https://app.example.com/cb&response_type=token&state=wapt HTTP/1.1
Host: idp.example.com
Connection: close
variants.expect: Must refuse response_type=token / id_token for a confidential app. implicit is deprecated.

variants.name: Token in query
variants.payload: After login, inspect the browser URL, any next= redirect, and the network log for access_token=.
variants.expect: Tokens belong in a POST body or a cookie, not a query string.

checks.title: SAML signature required
checks.why: The ACS accepts an unsigned or wrapped assertion.
checks.validate: A modified assertion (changed NameID or attribute) is accepted. Use a test IdP / your own assertion, never a real user's.

variants.name: Drop the signature
variants.payload: Capture a test-IdP SAMLResponse, remove ds:Signature, and POST it to the ACS.
variants.expect: Must reject. Do this only with a test account and a test IdP.

variants.name: Change NameID with signature left intact
variants.payload: Alter the NameID of a test assertion without recomputing the signature.
variants.expect: Must reject. Signature wrapping (signed wrapper, unsigned inner assertion) is the same class.

checks.title: RelayState / post-SSO navigation
checks.why: RelayState is an open redirect after a successful SSO.
checks.validate: The browser ends on an origin you control after a valid SSO.

variants.name: Absolute RelayState
variants.payload:
POST /sso/acs HTTP/1.1
Host: www.example.com
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

SAMLResponse=<valid-test>&RelayState=https%3A%2F%2Fevil.example%2F
variants.expect: Must stay on-origin. Repeat for //evil.example/ and /\evil.example/.

variants.name: Protocol-relative
variants.expect: Same check as any other open redirect. Confirm the final Location.
